text: The well was drilled to 990 m but due to failed cement operation of the surface casing, the well was abandoned.
Fishing was unsuccessful and the well was plugged back and technically sidetracked from 1443 m.
The primary objective was to test the Eocene sandstones that were gas bearing in well 25/1-1.
At the same time mud losses were experienced.
No shallow gas was observed, but the pilot BHA got stuck and had to be left in hole with top at 755 m.
It is possible that both a gas-oil contact and an oil-water contact occur in this zone, however, data available suggested tight formation.

text: Seventy-four meter below the 20" casing shoe, after the well had penetrated a fault at 954 m, high background gas with heavy components was encountered.
After several attempts of cutting, the string parted in the section of drill collars.
Junk was fished out of the hole before and after performing a leak off test below the 20" casing shoe.
The sample contained mud filtrate and formation water with no associated gas.
Logs and RFT pressure gradient proved Sleipner water filled, and ca 3 bar overpressured compared to the Hugin Formation.
The well was drilled with RheGuard oil-based mud from kick-off to TD.
During setting of the 7" liner for testing of the hydrocarbon zone, the pipe got stuck and broke between the extension pipe and drill string.
While circulating bottoms up for samples a kick was taken.
A study of wire line logs, sidewalls cores and hole response indicate that the gas was overpressured, and trapped in a non-reservoir lithology.
The mud weight was cut and LCM pills spotted at 2619 m to cure lost circulation problems.
Pipe stuck in the 12 1/4" hole at 2254 m and several times in the 8 1/2" hole.
Boulders were encountered drilling the 36" section, and was the main reason why the 22" underreamer became stuck in 20" casing.
The well was drilled with "Glydril" mud (KCl / Polymer / glycol) from kick-off to TD.
This led to lost circulation, but control was gradually regained after pumping LCM pills.
The well was permanently abandoned on 26 November as a gas/condensate discovery.
The well was then sidetracked again to 2220 m at which point the string got stuck again.
Scattered boulders could be expected between 424and 540 m.
There were no oil shows above the OBM in the well and the only significant formation gas in the well was a 63.2% gas peak at 2674 m, believed to be related to a fault.
Mud losses were experienced when increasing the mud weight.
Lost circulation was experienced in the 17 ½" hole, otherwise operations proceeded without significant problems.
It produced 26900 Sm3 /day gas with a water cut of 25% through a 36/64" choke.
The drill pipe became stuck at 486 m and the hole was abandoned with the top of fish at 323 m.
The drill string got mechanically stuck three times in the interval 2465 m to 2571 m, but came free within short time.
During well completion and preparation for production testing the screen-packer stuck at 570 m.
During the subsequent landing of the BOP on the well head, the ball joint parted, and the BOP fell down on the wellhead.
No shallow gas was encountered.
It produced 712 Sm3 oil and 84400 Sm3 gas /day through a 48/64" choke.
The run was aborted, the cable was disconnected and pulled out of the hole and the tool string was left in the hole.
An extensive sequence of permeable sands and silts were penetrated, without returns to surface, in the upper part of the well.
A 2.7% mud gas peak (methane) was recorded in this sand.
notes: 2.7% gas peak = hydrocarbon show, not a hazard

text: Average GOR was 120 m3/m3, oil Gravity was 0.82 g/cm3 (41.7 deg API) and the gas gravity was 0.712 (air = 1).
No coring was attempted in the upper section of this unit due to severe mud losses to the formation.
While drilling on with sea water, without returns, the pipe stuck.
Test no 3.1 tested the interval 2150 to 2161.5 m, which produced 1480 Sm3 oil and 70100 Sm3 gas /day through a 56/64" choke.
No shallow gas was seen, but lost circulation occurred in shallow sand lenses when the pilot was underreamed to 26".
Swelling clays (gumbo) caused some problems in the 17 1/2" section.
Some sand was found at the pre-warned level, but without shallow gas.
By repeated injection and partially circulation of kill mud through the perforations, the well was stabilized.
The top of the fish is left at 3910 m.
At 1426 m circulation was lost, and 450 bbls mud was lost to formation before the well was stabilized.
In addition the Utsira Formation was not logged due to a tight spot at 439 m.
No major problems occurred while drilling this well, but some tight hole problems were experienced in the 12 1/4" hole section.
The Sognefjord Formation reservoir was encountered with gas at 1691 m.
